sentences.text: The present appeal has been filed impugning the order of conviction dated 25.04.2023 and order on sentence dated 27.09.2023, passed by the learned Trial Court whereby the appellant herein has been held guilty for offences under Section 376, 417 and 471 IPC and sentenced, inter alia, for life imprisonment.
The sentences have been directed to run concurrently.
3. The above conviction and sentence have been passed in relation to FIR No.1199/2015, Police Station Saket.

4. According to appellant, he was, admittedly, released on bail in the present case for the period between 13.03.2020 to 12.04.2021 and 11.01.2022 to 29.04.2022 but since he was in custody in the other case, i.e., FIR No.654/2016, PS Neb Sarai for offences under Section 376/420 IPC, he continued to remain in prison and was not released and, therefore, the aforesaid period for which he was directed to be released on bail did not serve any purpose and, therefore, it is prayed that said period may be taken as custody period in the present case also and consequently, the benefit of remission may be granted to him.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant does not dispute that the appellant had submitted the bail bonds and even release warrants had been sent for his release for the above period.
However, her sole

It is in the aforesaid backdrop that she has prayed that period of around 16 months may be directed to be credited in his account as the period undergone by him in the present case pertaining to FIR No.1199/2015, Police Station Saket.
6. Reliance has been placed upon Niranjan Singh & Anr. Vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Ors.

sentences.text: 7. We have perused the aforesaid judgments relied upon by the learned counsel for the appellant.
However, we note that the factual matrix in the present case is totally different as here not only the bail bonds were submitted, even the release warrants were issued.
He could not be released as he was in custody in other case.

If at all the appellant was of the view that he was not going to be released because he was in judicial custody in some other case, he should not have submitted the bail bonds, without, at least, securing the bail order in said other case.
This is a digitally signed order.

In view of the above, we do not find any error in calculating the custody period of the applicant in FIR No.1199/2015, Police Station Saket and any reason to credit the custody period between 13.03.2020 to 12.04.2021 and 11.01.2022 to 29.04.2022 to the period of imprisonment already undergone by the applicant/appellant in the FIR No.1199/2015, Police Station Saket.
9.
The present application is, accordingly, dismissed.
